content.value_statement: Custom slash commands can become inconsistent, over-permissioned, or hard to test. This skill guides command creation with a template, least-privilege tool choices, and SlashCommand validation.
actual_capabilities: Reads the included command documentation and command template before drafting commands.
Chooses a project command location under .claude/commands/.
Creates or updates Markdown command files with YAML frontmatter and required sections.
Applies least-privilege allowed-tools guidance for new command definitions.
Tests generated commands through the SlashCommand tool when available.
limitations: It only covers custom slash command files, not general shell scripts or aliases.
It depends on Write and SlashCommand permissions in the active tool environment.
It does not validate command behavior beyond the available SlashCommand test.
It should not create personal commands outside the project command directory.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Commands
use_cases.description: Engineering leads can create shared project commands with consistent frontmatter, permissions, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Workflows
use_cases.description: Developers can revise command files while preserving the expected template structure and least-privilege tool rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: AI workflow maintainers can turn recurring prompts into reusable commands for Claude Code sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project slash command named [name] for [task]. Use the included template and choose the least permissions needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a simple reusable project command.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current command at [path]. Update it for [new behavior] while preserving frontmatter, rules, and acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Revise an existing command without losing structure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Team Workflow Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a shared command for [workflow]. Include clear phases, argument hints, allowed tools, and test it with SlashCommand.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a command for a recurring team workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refine Command Permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the command for [workflow]. Reduce tool permissions, clarify prohibited actions, update acceptance criteria, and run the available SlashCommand test.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an advanced command before sharing it.

output_examples.input: Create a command for reviewing pull requests before merge.
output: A project command plan with name, purpose, frontmatter fields, least-privilege tools, workflow phases, rules, and acceptance criteria.
A validation note showing the SlashCommand test result or the reason testing was unavailable.

output_examples.input: Update our release checklist command to include security review.
output_examples.output: A revised command structure that keeps existing sections, adds security review tasks, and records the validation result.

output_examples.input: Check whether this command grants too many tools.
output_examples.output: A permission review that identifies broad tool access, suggests narrower entries, and keeps only tools required for the workflow.

best_practices: Keep commands concise and focused on one repeatable workflow.
Grant only the tools needed for the command task.
Test each command after creation or update, then report the result.
anti_patterns: Creating commands with broad tool permissions when narrow rules would work.
Saving commands outside the approved project command directory.
Skipping the template sections or leaving placeholders in final commands.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates custom slash command Markdown files for Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it manage built-in slash commands?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on user-defined custom slash command files.

faq.question: Can it create personal commands in the home directory?
faq.answer: The skill constraints keep commands inside the project .claude/commands/ directory.

faq.question: How does it handle permissions?
faq.answer: It selects least-privilege allowed-tools entries based on the command job.

faq.question: Does it test commands?
faq.answer: It uses the SlashCommand tool when available and reports the result.

faq.question: Can teams use these commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Project commands stored in the repository can be shared with the team.
